WITH samples AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value, LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'key_on' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
)
SELECT ts / 1000.0 AS time, 'key on' AS text
FROM samples
WHERE value = 1 AND (previous IS NULL OR previous = 0)
ORDER BY time

WITH samples AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value, LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'go' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
)
SELECT ts / 1000.0 AS time, 'GO' AS text
FROM samples
WHERE value = 1 AND (previous IS NULL OR previous = 0)
ORDER BY time

-- 0x102 b2 bit0 used to feed this annotation under the name `charging`. It is the
-- HIGH BEAM (renamed high_beam_lamp 2026-08-16, see src/can/decode.ts), so every
-- flash-to-pass drew a charge marker. These two signals are the real thing, and it
-- takes both: bms_state_charge never fires on DC, because the BMS sits in Idle
-- through a fast charge, and fast_dc_contactor fires ONLY on DC.
WITH edges AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value,
         LAG(r.value) OVER (PARTITION BY s.key ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous,
         CASE s.key WHEN 'bms_state_charge' THEN 'Charge (BMS 0x201)'
                    ELSE 'DC fast charge (0x102 b3)' END AS label
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('bms_state_charge', 'fast_dc_contactor')
)
SELECT ts / 1000.0 AS time, label AS text
FROM edges
WHERE value = 1 AND (previous IS NULL OR previous <> 1)
  AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY ts

options.content:
### What is measured, and what is assumed

**Measured:** coolant inlet and outlet (2× PT100 on the custom battery loop), pack current and power, per-module temperatures from the BMS, inverter and motor temperatures, ambient from OBD-II.

**Assumed: the coolant flow rate.** It is not measured and it is not on the bus. Every “heat removed” figure below is `ΔT × k`, with `k = flow × ρ·cp` taken from the two boxes at the top of this dashboard. The defaults are 850 L/h — the duty point on the Bosch PAD 12 V pump datasheet (part 0 392 023 004, 850 dm³/h at 0.1 bar) — and 3.5 MJ·m⁻³·K⁻¹ for a 50/50 glycol/water mix. The loop's actual restriction is unknown, so the real flow sits somewhere below that. **The shape of the heat curve is trustworthy; the absolute scale is not.**

**Not claimed at all: heat in.** `pack_kw` is pack *terminal* power; only the I²R fraction of it ends up in the coolant. It is drawn next to ΔT so the correlation can speak for itself — no watts figure for heat in is asserted anywhere on this dashboard.

panels.title: Coolant loop — the custom watercooling on the battery pack

panels.description: Query returns a time column and a value column, so the stat panel gets a proper frame. Newest outlet−inlet pair in the window. Positive = the pack is putting heat into the coolant. Unlike the other ΔT panels this one does not skip unusable pairs: if the newest sample cannot be paired — a probe reading outside −20…100 °C, or silent for over an hour — the tile goes blank rather than showing the last good value.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH probe_samples AS (
  -- Two columns per probe on purpose. `*_row` marks that the probe reported at all and
  -- drives the carry-forward partition; `inlet`/`outlet` carry the value only when it is
  -- in range. An out-of-range reading therefore starts a new partition holding NULL, so the
  -- hold yields NULL rather than the last good value. That removes the fabricated movement
  -- the old filter produced (a stuck probe drove ΔT 0.5 -> 0.6 -> 0.7). Where the row is then
  -- dropped, that is all it does: spanNulls bridges the missing rows exactly the way it bridges
  -- a quiet period, so the trace still holds flat. Two panels go further and show the fault
  -- itself -- the 'ΔT latest' tile blanks, and 'ΔT across the pack' keeps the row as an explicit
  -- NULL with spanNulls off so it draws as a gap. Ingest already
  -- gates at -40..150 (max31865.ts), so this narrower band is about the derived maths only;
  -- the raw coolant traces are plotted unfiltered so a fault is visible there as itself.
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.rowid AS rid,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_in' THEN 1 END AS inlet_row,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_out' THEN 1 END AS outlet_row,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_in' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END AS inlet,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END AS outlet,
         -- the sample's own timestamp, carried forward with the value so the pairing can
         -- expire. See the `paired` CTE below.
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_in' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END AS inlet_at,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END AS outlet_at
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('coolant_in', 'coolant_out')
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  UNION ALL
  -- Seed the hold with each probe's last sample from before the window. Without this,
  -- zooming to a stretch where only one probe happened to log a change leaves the other
  -- NULL and every ΔT-derived panel reads "No data" at once, despite both values being
  -- known. Seed rows are filtered back out of the final SELECT by `ts >= $__from`.
  -- One ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 per probe rather than a ROW_NUMBER() over everything before
  -- the window: this is a backwards seek on idx_reading_sig_ts that stops after one row,
  -- so it stays flat as the file grows instead of walking every earlier coolant sample.
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT r.ts, r.rowid, 1, NULL,
           CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END, NULL,
           CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END, NULL
    FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
    -- capped lookback: without it a 5-minute window can pair a fresh outlet reading with
    -- an inlet operand from hours earlier (one probe silent across a shutdown), producing a
    -- large fake ΔT and a large fake heat figure at a real timestamp. Past an hour the
    -- honest answer is no reading rather than a stale one.
    WHERE s.key = 'coolant_in' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts >= $__from - 3600000
    ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1
  )
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT r.ts, r.rowid, NULL, 1,
           NULL, CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END,
           NULL, CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END
    FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
    WHERE s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts >= $__from - 3600000
    ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1
  )
),
runs AS (
  SELECT ts, inlet, outlet, inlet_at, outlet_at,
         COUNT(inlet_row) OVER (ORDER BY ts, rid ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS inlet_run,
         COUNT(outlet_row) OVER (ORDER BY ts, rid ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS outlet_run
  FROM probe_samples
),
held AS (
  SELECT ts,
         MAX(inlet) OVER (PARTITION BY inlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS inlet_held,
         MAX(outlet) OVER (PARTITION BY outlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS outlet_held,
         MAX(inlet_at) OVER (PARTITION BY inlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS inlet_at_held,
         MAX(outlet_at) OVER (PARTITION BY outlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS outlet_at_held
  FROM runs
),
paired AS (
  -- A held value expires an hour after the sample it came from. The -20..100 guard above
  -- only catches a probe that reports bad numbers; a probe that goes fully open stops
  -- reporting at all, because max31865.ts skips the read rather than clamping it. Without
  -- an expiry its last good value would keep pairing with fresh readings from the other
  -- probe for the rest of the window and draw a confident, entirely fabricated ΔT -- and a
  -- fabricated heat figure with it. One hour, applied to every row rather than only to the
  -- seed, which is why the seed's own lower bound is belt-and-braces (it still narrows the
  -- index range, so it stays).
  -- The hour is calibrated against the PER-PROBE inter-sample gap, which is the thing this
  -- test measures -- not the gap between ΔT points, which only needs one probe to report.
  -- Over the 2026-08-02 file: coolant_in 466 gaps, longest 23.6 min; coolant_out 322 gaps,
  -- longest 23.3 min; neither has a single gap over an hour. Note that file is 4.8 h of a
  -- mostly-parked bike and contains no overnight sit, so if a healthy long window ever reads
  -- "No data", this constant is the first thing to re-measure.
  SELECT ts,
         CASE WHEN ts - inlet_at_held <= 3600000 THEN inlet_held END AS inlet_held,
         CASE WHEN ts - outlet_at_held <= 3600000 THEN outlet_held END AS outlet_held
  FROM held
  ORDER BY ts
)
-- no IS NOT NULL filter, unlike the other ΔT panels: this tile is about the latest
-- pairing specifically, so if the newest sample cannot be paired the tile should go
-- blank rather than quietly serve the last good ΔT. Now that the hold is seeded from
-- before the window, a NULL here means a faulted probe, not "the other one is late".
SELECT ts / 1000.0 AS time, outlet_held - inlet_held AS value
FROM paired
WHERE ts >= $__from
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 1

panels.title: ΔT latest

panels.description: Query returns a time column and a value column, so the stat panel gets a proper frame. Largest outlet−inlet in the window, among pairings still fresh enough to use. A held reading expires an hour after the sample it came from, so a pairing staler than that is dropped rather than counted. The tile shows the value only; the query returns the instant too, but textMode is "value" so it is not drawn.

panels.title: ΔT peak

panels.description: Query returns a time column and a value column, so the stat panel gets a proper frame. Most negative outlet−inlet, among pairings still fresh enough to use. A held reading expires an hour after the sample it came from, so a pairing staler than that is dropped rather than counted. panels.title: Heat removed, peak (assumed flow)

panels.description: Query returns a time column and a value column, so the stat panel gets a proper frame. Hottest outlet reading in the window.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts / 1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
-- unfiltered: ingest already gates at -40..150 (max31865.ts) by skipping the read,
-- so a degraded probe reading 100..150 reaches the DB and should land on the >=60
-- purple band rather than be discarded here. A fully open RTD reads wilder than that
-- and is never recorded at all, so its signature is the trace stopping, not a spike.
WHERE s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.value DESC
LIMIT 1

panels.title: Coolant outlet, peak

panels.description: Query returns a time column and a value column, so the stat panel gets a proper frame. OBD-II PID 46. Every temperature on the bike converges on this once it has been parked long enough.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts / 1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'ambient_temp' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC
LIMIT 1

panels.title: Ambient, latest

panels.description: The two PT100 probes on the custom battery loop, plus ambient (OBD-II PID 46, 1 °C resolution) as the reference every temperature decays towards when the bike is parked. Signals are logged on change with a deadband, so a flat line means “unchanged”, not “not measured” — hence step interpolation and spanNulls (a gap is held at the last value, not drawn as a dip). Nothing is filtered here: ingest already rejects reads outside −40…150 °C (max31865.ts), so anything that reaches the database was kept deliberately and a degraded probe draws as the excursion it is. SELECT r.ts / 1000.0 AS time, s.key AS metric, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
-- unfiltered: ingest already gates at -40..150 (max31865.ts) by skipping the read.
-- A degraded probe still inside that band is a fault worth drawing, not one worth
-- hiding. A fully open RTD never reaches the DB, so it shows up as the trace stopping.
WHERE s.key IN ('coolant_in', 'coolant_out', 'ambient_temp')
  AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Coolant inlet and outlet, against ambient

panels.description: The one directly measured cooling quantity. Both probes are logged on change and never share a timestamp, so each point pairs a fresh reading from one probe with the last known reading of the other (carry-forward). That is not a synchronised pair — a fast transient can show up on one side one sample before the other. Pairing strictly by 10 s bucket instead would leave 60 points where this leaves 789. A held reading expires an hour after the sample it came from, so a pairing staler than that is dropped rather than counted. Unlike the other panels here this one keeps those rows and emits a null, and turns spanNulls off, so a probe fault draws as a gap rather than as a flat line indistinguishable from a quiet period. Near zero, ΔT is dominated by the probes' mutual offset rather than by heat transfer.

WITH probe_samples AS (
  -- Two columns per probe on purpose. `*_row` marks that the probe reported at all and
  -- drives the carry-forward partition; `inlet`/`outlet` carry the value only when it is
  -- in range. An out-of-range reading therefore starts a new partition holding NULL, so the
  -- hold yields NULL rather than the last good value. That removes the fabricated movement
  -- the old filter produced (a stuck probe drove ΔT 0.5 -> 0.6 -> 0.7). Where the row is then
  -- dropped, that is all it does: spanNulls bridges the missing rows exactly the way it bridges
  -- a quiet period, so the trace still holds flat. Two panels go further and show the fault
  -- itself -- the 'ΔT latest' tile blanks, and 'ΔT across the pack' keeps the row as an explicit
  -- NULL with spanNulls off so it draws as a gap. Ingest already
  -- gates at -40..150 (max31865.ts), so this narrower band is about the derived maths only;
  -- the raw coolant traces are plotted unfiltered so a fault is visible there as itself.
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.rowid AS rid,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_in' THEN 1 END AS inlet_row,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_out' THEN 1 END AS outlet_row,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_in' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END AS inlet,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END AS outlet,
         -- the sample's own timestamp, carried forward with the value so the pairing can
         -- expire. See the `paired` CTE below.
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_in' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END AS inlet_at,
         CASE WHEN s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END AS outlet_at
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('coolant_in', 'coolant_out')
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  UNION ALL
  -- Seed the hold with each probe's last sample from before the window. Without this,
  -- zooming to a stretch where only one probe happened to log a change leaves the other
  -- NULL and every ΔT-derived panel reads "No data" at once, despite both values being
  -- known. Seed rows are filtered back out of the final SELECT by `ts >= $__from`.
  -- One ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 per probe rather than a ROW_NUMBER() over everything before
  -- the window: this is a backwards seek on idx_reading_sig_ts that stops after one row,
  -- so it stays flat as the file grows instead of walking every earlier coolant sample.
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT r.ts, r.rowid, 1, NULL,
           CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END, NULL,
           CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END, NULL
    FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
    -- capped lookback: without it a 5-minute window can pair a fresh outlet reading with
    -- an inlet operand from hours earlier (one probe silent across a shutdown), producing a
    -- large fake ΔT and a large fake heat figure at a real timestamp. Past an hour the
    -- honest answer is no reading rather than a stale one.
    WHERE s.key = 'coolant_in' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts >= $__from - 3600000
    ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1
  )
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT r.ts, r.rowid, NULL, 1,
           NULL, CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.value END,
           NULL, CASE WHEN r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100 THEN r.ts END
    FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
    WHERE s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.ts < $__from AND r.ts >= $__from - 3600000
    ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1
  )
),
runs AS (
  SELECT ts, inlet, outlet, inlet_at, outlet_at,
         COUNT(inlet_row) OVER (ORDER BY ts, rid ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS inlet_run,
         COUNT(outlet_row) OVER (ORDER BY ts, rid ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS outlet_run
  FROM probe_samples
),
held AS (
  SELECT ts,
         MAX(inlet) OVER (PARTITION BY inlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS inlet_held,
         MAX(outlet) OVER (PARTITION BY outlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS outlet_held,
         MAX(inlet_at) OVER (PARTITION BY inlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS inlet_at_held,
         MAX(outlet_at) OVER (PARTITION BY outlet_run ORDER BY ts) AS outlet_at_held
  FROM runs
),
paired AS (
  -- A held value expires an hour after the sample it came from. The -20..100 guard above
  -- only catches a probe that reports bad numbers; a probe that goes fully open stops
  -- reporting at all, because max31865.ts skips the read rather than clamping it. Without
  -- an expiry its last good value would keep pairing with fresh readings from the other
  -- probe for the rest of the window and draw a confident, entirely fabricated ΔT -- and a
  -- fabricated heat figure with it. One hour, applied to every row rather than only to the
  -- seed, which is why the seed's own lower bound is belt-and-braces (it still narrows the
  -- index range, so it stays).
  -- The hour is calibrated against the PER-PROBE inter-sample gap, which is the thing this
  -- test measures -- not the gap between ΔT points, which only needs one probe to report.
  -- Over the 2026-08-02 file: coolant_in 466 gaps, longest 23.6 min; coolant_out 322 gaps,
  -- longest 23.3 min; neither has a single gap over an hour. Note that file is 4.8 h of a
  -- mostly-parked bike and contains no overnight sit, so if a healthy long window ever reads
  -- "No data", this constant is the first thing to re-measure.
  SELECT ts,
         CASE WHEN ts - inlet_at_held <= 3600000 THEN inlet_held END AS inlet_held,
         CASE WHEN ts - outlet_at_held <= 3600000 THEN outlet_held END AS outlet_held
  FROM held
  ORDER BY ts
)
-- Unusable pairings are kept and emitted as NULL rather than filtered out, and this panel
-- alone sets spanNulls: false. Filtering plus spanNulls renders a fault identically to a
-- deadband quiet period -- one flat step across it either way. Keeping the row makes the
-- distinction structural instead of threshold-based: rows exist only where a probe actually
-- sampled, so a NULL means "sampled, could not be paired" (fault) while ordinary quiet
-- produces no row at all and still connects. Checked in a Grafana 11.3 container that the
-- datasource returns config {} on the time field -- no frame interval, so Grafana does not
-- auto-insert nulls into gaps and spanNulls: false breaks only where a NULL really is.
SELECT ts / 1000.0 AS time, 'delta_t' AS metric, outlet_held - inlet_held AS value
FROM paired
WHERE ts >= $__from
ORDER BY time

panels.title: ΔT across the pack (outlet − inlet)
Heat balance — ΔT is measured, flow is assumed

panels.description:
Left axis: ΔT × k, where k = flow × ρ·cp comes from the dashboard variables. Flow is an assumption (Bosch PAD 12 V datasheet duty point, 850 dm³/h at 0.1 bar); the loop's restriction is unknown, so the real flow is lower and so is the real heat. The curve's shape follows ΔT exactly — only its scale is guesswork. A held reading expires an hour after the sample it came from, so a pairing staler than that is dropped rather than counted.

Right axis: `pack_kw` straight off the BMS, on its own axis because it is two orders of magnitude larger. It is terminal power, NOT heat input — only the I²R share of it turns into heat, and that share is not known here. Negative = discharging. Compare the shapes, not the numbers. panels.title: ΔT vs pack current² (I²R loss proxy)
Pack modules — 31 temperature sensors across 11 LMUs

panels.description:
One row per module sensor: `bat1` is the cell-pack thermistor, `pcb1`/`pcb2` sit on the module board. Colour is temperature, banded rather than continuous because the BMS reports whole degrees. Reading across a column tells you which module runs hottest.

Nothing is filtered. Purple (≥60 °C) is not a real temperature — it is a dead or open sensor. In the 2026-08-02 file LMU07 bat1 and LMU09 bat1 both sit at a flat 122 °C for roughly 50 minutes while the pack is at 28 °C; clipping that away would hide a fault, so it is left in and given its own colour.

Values are logged on change, so a bar runs until the sensor next reports something different. That means a sensor that has stopped reporting entirely looks exactly like one sitting at a steady temperature, and no threshold on this panel can separate them: in the 2026-08-02 file a healthy module goes 48 minutes between logged samples at a constant 28 °C, so any “gone quiet” cutoff short enough to catch a real dropout would fire on settled modules constantly. The signal that does distinguish them is lmu_comm_warnings (0x206), on the Isolation & faults dashboard.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts / 1000.0 AS time, printf('LMU%02d %s', CAST(substr(s.key, 4, instr(s.key, '_') - 4) AS INTEGER), replace(substr(s.key, instr(s.key, '_') + 1), '_c', '')) AS metric, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key GLOB 'lmu[0-9]*_c' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Per-module temperature

panels.description: Which module sensor ran hottest in the window, sorted by peak. Sorting by peak also puts failed sensors at the top, which is the point — a 122 °C peak next to a 28 °C mean is an open thermistor, not a hot module. `samples` is the number of logged changes, so a low count means the sensor barely moved (or barely reported).

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT printf('LMU%02d %s', CAST(substr(s.key, 4, instr(s.key, '_') - 4) AS INTEGER), replace(substr(s.key, instr(s.key, '_') + 1), '_c', '')) AS sensor,
       COUNT(*) AS samples,
       MIN(r.value) AS min_c,
       AVG(r.value) AS mean_c,
       MAX(r.value) AS max_c,
       (SELECT r2.value FROM reading r2
         WHERE r2.signal_id = s.id AND r2.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
         ORDER BY r2.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_c
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key GLOB 'lmu[0-9]*_c' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
GROUP BY s.id
ORDER BY max_c DESC, sensor

panels.title: Hottest module sensor

panels.description:
Every way the bike reports pack temperature, side by side with the coolant probes, with nothing filtered or smoothed — so decoder and frame problems stay visible instead of being averaged away.

What to look for: `batt_temp_hi`/`lo` are supposed to be the TRUE pack temperature and `*_vcu` the VCU's 15 °C-shifted view. Whenever the true pair lands exactly on the `_vcu` pair, the decoder has fallen back to 0x200 and is showing the shifted value — that is a decoding artefact, not the pack cooling by 15 °C. In the 2026-08-02 file that happens between roughly 15:04 and 16:20 UTC. A lone 0 °C in `pack_temp_avg` is a dropped frame, same story. Signals are logged on change with a deadband, so a flat line means “unchanged”, not “not measured” — hence step interpolation and spanNulls (a gap is held at the last value, not drawn as a dip).

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts / 1000.0 AS time, s.key AS metric, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key IN ('batt_temp_hi', 'batt_temp_lo', 'batt_temp_hi_vcu', 'batt_temp_lo_vcu', 'pack_temp_avg',
                'coolant_in', 'coolant_out')
  AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Pack temperature sources, unfiltered

panels.description:
The four channels of CAN 0x020 plus the motor sensor from 0x022. The IGBT trio is by far the most responsive thermal signal on the bike — on one slow garage lap it moved 10.6 °C while the motor moved 0.6 °C and the coolant 3 °C — so it gets its own left axis. Gate, motor and ambient share the right axis; putting all six on one axis would flatten the IGBT movement into a straight line.

0x020 reports IGBT min, instantaneous and max, but they have not yet been seen to separate from each other, so expect three lines on top of one another until a real load run says otherwise. Signals are logged on change with a deadband, so a flat line means “unchanged”, not “not measured” — hence step interpolation and spanNulls (a gap is held at the last value, not drawn as a dip).

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts / 1000.0 AS time, s.key AS metric, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key IN ('inverter_igbt_min_c', 'inverter_igbt_c', 'inverter_igbt_max_c', 'inverter_gate_c',
                'motor_temp_c', 'ambient_temp')
  AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Inverter IGBT (left) · gate, motor and ambient (right)

panels.description: The factory motor/inverter loop, which is separate from the battery loop the ΔT panels are about. Polled at 1 Hz over OBD-II: PID 05 (`bike_coolant_temp`), PID 5C (`oil_temp`) and PID 46 (ambient), all at 1 °C resolution, so the traces are stepped by the sensor and not just by the logger. Signals are logged on change with a deadband, so a flat line means “unchanged”, not “not measured” — hence step interpolation and spanNulls (a gap is held at the last value, not drawn as a dip).

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts / 1000.0 AS time, s.key AS metric, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key IN ('bike_coolant_temp', 'oil_temp', 'ambient_temp')
  AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Bike's own cooling loop (OBD-II)

list.description: ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. There is no flow sensor in the loop and no flow signal on the bus. 850 dm³/h is the duty point on the Bosch PAD 12 V pump datasheet (0 392 023 004) at 0.1 bar; the loop's real restriction is unknown, so the actual flow is lower. Change this and every heat figure rescales.

list.description: ASSUMPTION. 3.5 MJ·m⁻³·K⁻¹ is roughly a 50/50 ethylene-glycol/water mix near 30 °C (≈ 1060 kg/m³ × 3.3 kJ/kg/K). Straight water would be about 4.2.
